name: Class H Entry Permit (Ordinary Resident, Self-Sufficient/Retiree)

requirements.blocker_text: Assured annual income of at least US$36,000 derived from sources outside Uganda.
requirements.fix_path: Secure and document at least US$36,000/year in income from outside Uganda.

requirements.blocker_text: Signed pledge not to accept employment or engage in income-generating activities while in Uganda.

evidence_required.document: Police clearance / Interpol certificate (within last 6 months)

sources.title: Directorate of Citizenship and Immigration Control, Uganda -- Class H Entry Permit (Ordinary Resident): for persons with assured income from sources outside Uganda who undertake not to seek employment; requires proof of annual income of at least US$36,000; fees USD 750 (6mo) to 4,500 (36mo)

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Uganda). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- tier-1 DCIC sourced, directly fetched by me. This is Uganda's functional equivalent of a retiree/self-sufficient-income residence route (comparable to Nigeria's N5A/N5B retirement visas or Fiji's Residence Permit on Assured Income) -- 'ordinary resident' is the source's own term, not restricted to retirees specifically, but the no-employment pledge and foreign-income requirement produce the same practical profile. No age floor was found (unlike Nigeria's 65+ or Fiji's 45+ equivalents) -- this route appears open to any age group meeting the income threshold, a genuinely distinctive structural difference worth flagging. leads_to_pr/pr_after_months modeled as immediate/renewable-indefinitely in practice since the permit itself functions as ongoing residence status as long as renewed, though it does not itself convert into a separate formal 'permanent residence' status distinct from repeated Class H renewal -- this is an interpretation, not an explicit tier-1 statement.
